supersedes.what_failed: F2_CROSS_VERSION_EVIDENCE detected 18 of 49 injections (0.367), against a preregistered minimum of 1.0.
supersedes.diagnosis: The failure was in the harness, not in the contract. The V01 injector always mutated blocks[0], but a case's bindings do not necessarily cite blocks[0]. Partitioning the 49 cases by whether the mutated block was cited gives a perfect diagonal: cited and detected 18, cited and missed 0, uncited and detected 0, uncited and missed 31. Every injection that was actually witnessed by a binding was caught; every miss was an injection into evidence no binding cited, which the contract is not asked to check.
supersedes.why_v01_is_not_deleted: The FAIL verdict and its receipt stay on the record. A harness defect that produced a real FAIL is evidence about how this measurement was built, and removing it would leave only the passing run visible.

question: On canonical documents built from real parser output, does the Semantic Preservation Contract detect injected evidence faults in cited evidence, and is the repair scope it reports local to the damage?

change_from_v01.only_change: F2 now mutates the SourceRef of a block that some binding actually cites, selected as the first block appearing in any binding's source_block_ids, rather than unconditionally blocks[0].
unchanged: F1, F3, F4 injectors are byte-identical to V01
document and binding construction is byte-identical to V01
the negative control is byte-identical to V01
all preregistered gate thresholds are byte-identical to V01
change_from_v01.note: The gate F2 failed against is retained unchanged at 1.0. If the fix is wrong, this experiment fails the same gate again.

inputs.case_selection: every case with status == completed and block_count >= 4, ordered by case_id; no sampling
inputs.provenance_note: Read-only. Writes nothing into SEM-RISK-CONF-02 and consumes none of its inference budget.

fault_families.injection: a binding cites a block id that is not present in the document
the SourceRef of a block that a binding cites is rewritten to a different document_version_id
a binding cites a table cell that belongs to no attached source block
a declared critical token is removed from the evidence text it was drawn from

negative_control.description: the unmodified document, run through the same path

additional_control_from_v01.description: mutate the version of a block that no binding cites; the contract should stay silent
additional_control_from_v01.why: V01's failure showed this behaviour accidentally. Stating it as an explicit expectation turns an artifact into a measured boundary: the contract's scope is cited evidence, and this control documents that it does not silently extend beyond it.

metrics.detection_rate_per_family: detected / injected, reported separately for each fault family
metrics.false_positive_rate: clean documents reporting any violation / clean documents
metrics.uncited_mutation_false_positive_rate: N1 controls reporting any violation / N1 controls
metrics.repair_locality_blocks: quarantined blocks / total blocks, per detected fault
metrics.repair_locality_pages: quarantined pages / total pages, per detected fault

limitations: Faults are injected synthetically; the detection rate is over injected faults, not over faults observed in the wild.
The corpus is Lane A born-digital pages; image-only pages are not represented.
Critical tokens are derived mechanically from evidence text rather than declared by a domain expert.
F3 injects a detached cell id rather than constructing a full table, so it exercises the cell-attachment check but not table reconstruction.
